summary: This script automates a deployment workflow: it verifies that required tools are installed, pulls the latest code, builds a Docker image tagged with the current commit hash, starts the application container, then polls a health endpoint up to 12 times to confirm the deployment succeeded before exiting.

explanations.2: This line makes the script exit immediately if any command fails, treats undefined variables as errors, and prevents pipes from silently failing partway through — it's a safety net for scripting.
explanations.5: The command -v checks if a tool exists in your system's PATH, and >/dev/null 2>&1 suppresses all output so we only care about the success or failure status.
explanations.13: This creates a Docker image tag by combining 'myapp:' with the short form of the current git commit hash, so each build gets a unique identifier tied to the code version.
explanations.16: We're passing the image tag as an environment variable to docker compose so it knows which image to run for the app service.
explanations.18: This loop runs 12 times (seq 1 12 generates numbers 1 through 12), giving the app up to a minute to become healthy since each iteration sleeps 5 seconds.
explanations.19: curl -w '%{http_code}' extracts just the HTTP status code from the response, and we check if it equals 200 to confirm the health endpoint is returning success.
